description:
The fourth READ reports '04', a record-length conflict - which is what a stored row whose length disagrees with the 500-byte record area looks like to the program. It reaches the WHEN OTHER arm of the read's guard chain at app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl:L101 from a status no other case in this folder uses, and it reaches it after real output has already been produced: L93 READ is neither '00' at L94 nor '10' at L98, so L101 moves 12 into APPL-RESULT, the 88 APPL-AOK test at L104 fails, the 88 APPL-EOF test at L107 fails too, and the fatal arm runs - DISPLAY 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' at L110, MOVE CUSTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS at L111, PERFORM Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at L112 and PERFORM Z-ABEND-PROGRAM at L113. The six record lines before the failure are part of the expectation, not noise: a mainframe spool holds whatever a job displayed before it abended, so a translation that buffered its output and discarded it on the abend would be wrong. There are six rather than three because CBCUS01C displays every record TWICE - once at L96 inside the '00' arm of 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT and again at L78 in the mainline. That doubling is a genuine per-program inconsistency (CBACT02C has its L96 display commented out altogether) and is preserved rather than harmonised, per practice B5. Each line is the raw 500-character group image byte for byte, including the 168 spaces of CVCUS01Y's trailing FILLER. RETURN-CODE is 12, and it is derived rather than assumed: L101's MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT is the value standing in APPL-RESULT when CALL 'CEE3ABD' is reached at L158, alongside MOVE 0 TO TIMING at L156 and MOVE 999 TO ABCODE at L157. It is NOT 8 - that is the pessimistic pre-set the open makes at L119, overwritten at L122 on the successful open this case has, and never observable. It is NOT 16 - that is APPL-EOF, an internal state reached only by a '10' read, and this run never reaches end-of-file. It is NOT 0, which only L87's GOBACK produces. Only 0 and 12 are derivable from this program at all. The literal NNNN in 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0004' is GENUINE EXPECTED OUTPUT and must not be 'corrected'. Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS codes DISPLAY 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' IO-STATUS-04 at both L168 and L172, and the four characters NNNN are placeholder text the author never substituted: COBOL emits the literal verbatim and then appends the operand, so the emitted line carries both. Anyone reading this fixture should treat NNNN as inherited behaviour (practice B5), never as a placeholder left behind by a case author (practice B1). The value is rendered through the numeric branch. '04' is all-numeric and its first byte is '0' and not '9', so L162's class condition is false and the paragraph takes its ELSE arm at L170-L172: MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04 then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), overlaying the two status characters at one-based positions three and four to give 0004. IO-STATUS-04 is read mechanically from the WORKING-STORAGE declaration at L57-L59 as IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 (practice B11). case09 drives this same paragraph's ELSE arm from a failed OPEN with '35', and case08, case10, case16 and case17 drive the IO-STAT1 = '9' arm at L162-L168; what this case uniquely owns is the '04' status itself, which no other case in the folder reports at any call site. The message text names the file the long way. The read and close paragraphs say 'CUSTOMER FILE' - L110 and L147 - while the open paragraph at L129 names the DD instead, 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE'. The wording is inconsistent in the source and is reproduced exactly as each paragraph has it. The closing banner at L85 is not emitted, and neither is a close message of any kind. CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L158 terminates the enclave, so control never returns to L113's caller: 9000-CUSTFILE-CLOSE at L83 never runs and L85 is never reached. A case that appended that banner because the run had 'finished' would be asserting a line the abend makes unreachable, so the banner's literal text is deliberately absent from this file altogether - a reader grepping the fixture tree for it will not find it here, in an expectation or in prose. expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are both empty, and no expectedDatasets is declared, because this case arranges a backend failure: the run meets a stubbed customer master rather than a stored relation, so no final state is read back and none is reported. An empty expectation is a positive assertion that nothing was produced on that channel, so declaring the seeded rows here would assert output the arranged path never reports and would fail the diff. The clean-path cases - case01 chief among them - own the stored-state assertions. Nothing is written in any event: CBCUS01C opens INPUT and issues no WRITE, no REWRITE and no DELETE. Five records are seeded although three are delivered, which pins two separate things: the run stops two records short of the end of the file, so it is the abend and not exhaustion that ends it, and the seed is large enough for the arranged failing read to be the fourth one rather than the file's last. The dataset is addressed by the binding key CUSTFILE alone - the name L29's SELECT ASSIGN TO gives it and the name app/jcl/READCUST.jcl STEP05 mounts on its single //CUSTFILE DD - so the DSNAME stays in configuration and never appears in a case (gate G46). That step declares no PARM anywhere, so jobParameters is empty. The fixture bytes are US-ASCII, named explicitly rather than left to a platform default (practice B8), and custdata.txt matches its copybook width exactly at 500 bytes, so this case declares no normalisation - only cardxref.txt needs the 36-to-50 FILLER pad. R1 caveat: the mandated name CustomerFileReaderJob names a Spring Batch job, but the source Function header reads 'Read and print customer data file' - it computes nothing and writes no dataset, so no output record is expected here. Baseline provenance (practice B12): these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the control flow of app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl, the byte layout app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy declares, the step and DD contract in app/jcl/READCUST.jcl and the real 50-row app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt fixture. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution - running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, as AAP section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers, and the substitution of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. Gates discharged: G15 (one of the twenty cases this program owns), G18 (the diff count must be zero across all twenty), G35 (the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L158 surfaces as an AbendException carrying RETURN-CODE 12, which the step reports as a non-zero exit status rather than an HTTP error), G47 (the '04' arm of the READ's guard chain - the one status in the WHEN OTHER family no other case in this folder exercises), G50 (88-level coverage in both states: APPL-AOK true for the three delivered reads and false for the fourth, APPL-EOF false throughout because end-of-file is never reached) and G51 (the job is driven at tasklet level with CustomerService as the decision-holding collaborator, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path).

HOW THE OUTCOME IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges a READ that fails after three records with a length conflict: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names READ-CUSTFILE and gives it FILE STATUS '04', reported after 3 record(s). It is declared here because a case identifier must name a case and never configure one - the arrangement used to live in a table in CBCUS01CParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', so this file showed the rendered status and the abend and said nothing about what produced them, and renumbering a case silently changed what it ran. A case that names no call site runs the ordinary path, so silence here is itself a statement.
